citation.title: Model-based estimation of tokamak plasma profiles and physics parameters: algorithm overview and application to ITER
citation.authors: Van Mulders S., Felici F., McIntosh S.C., Carpanese F., Contré C.E., Coosemans R., Kudlácek O., Pastore F., Pinches S.D., Reisner M., Sauter O.

topic: EKF/ERTSS state and parameter estimation of electron profiles and current density with RAPTOR, tested on synthetic ITER data
own_question: Can a transport-model-based EKF recover jpar, Te and ne evolution, plus parameters such as Zeff and transport coefficients, from noisy synthetic TS and boundary-flux measurements?
actual_method_and_evidence: The EKF combines RAPTOR physics predictions with noisy synthetic TS Te/ne and boundary-flux measurements. The measurements were made by adding white noise to a single DINA-JINTRAC Q=10 simulation; no experimental data were used. The authors report qualitative agreement with the simulation ground truth and RMSE traces. A cubic-spline interpolation in space and time (INTERPOS) slightly outperformed the EKF for Te recovery. A case with core TS dropped out is also shown. Smoothing (ERTSS) gave only modest gains.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Sequential Bayesian filters such as the EKF combine uncertain model predictions with noisy measurements. A filter uses only past and current data; a smoother also uses later data.
claim_checks.qualification: Conceptual background only. Their setting is electron profiles in a simulation study, not CES impurity Ti.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: In one synthetic ITER study, a non-model space-time spline interpolation recovered Te slightly better than a model-based EKF when measurements were dense.
claim_checks.qualification: Covers only synthetic white noise, dense TS and electron Te. This motivates comparing against interpolation baselines; it is not evidence about our data.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Inputs are synthetic TS at 0.5 s steps (one in 50 of the 10 ms TS samples) plus the boundary flux. Targets are simulated Te, ne and jpar. The reported ~240 s compute time for a 786 s discharge is offline, not a deployment result.
validation_if_relevant: Validation uses a single simulated discharge with known ground truth, with covariances tuned against that truth. There is no experimental or held-out data.
forbidden_inferences: Do not claim the paper addresses CES, impurity or ion temperature, BES/ECEI, or KSTAR.
Do not claim real-time deployment or experimental validation from this paper.
Do not claim model-based methods beat interpolation.
Do not generalize this paper to all prior work.
Do not treat simulation ground truth as analogous to our CES labels.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Include as background for filter versus smoother causality and for the value of an interpolation baseline. Keep it out of the direct-precedent framing.
